clue.text: With such skill we may make a packet!

definitions.text: With such skill we may make a packet!

parts.words: With such skill we may make a packet!
parts.note: a word for skill or artfulness is also a word for a boat, and a packet is an old mail boat, so this vessel-word is something a packet is

explanation.surface: A boast that our talent will earn us a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a packet' looks like earning lots of money; a packet is also a packet boat, a kind of vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both skill and a boat, and a packet boat is one such vessel.

clue.text: Civil Service girl with scope to enter instruction areas

indicators.note: the girl and the scope go into the abbreviation, so these words signal a container

parts.note: a lass is a girl
room means scope, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A government department official and a young woman with room to spare move into teaching spaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms where pupils are taught are areas set aside for instruction.

clue.text: Part of circle a councillor set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the councillor's abbreviation is written upwards, bottom to top

explanation.surface: A councillor erects part of a circular structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved section of a circle's circumference is called by this geometric term.

clue.text: Tool found in river, wrapped in absorbent cloth

indicators.note: the river letter sits wrapped inside the cloth, signalling a container

parts.note: a towel is an absorbent cloth

explanation.surface: An implement discovered in a stream, bundled up in a bath sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand implement used by gardeners and bricklayers, so it is an example of a tool.

clue.text: Thus woman frames old questionin in dramatic speech

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: the woman's name surrounds the other letters like a picture frame, signalling a container

parts.note: Lily is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman puts an old question into a speech from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech in a play spoken by a character alone, voicing thoughts aloud to the audience.

clue.text: Somehow mine fails to make late stage in contest

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: A mine somehow fails, ruining a team's run deep into a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The round just before the final is a late stage in a knockout contest.

clue.text: Start off without a meal

indicators.note: without means the letter a is left out of the longer word

parts.note: to launch is to start something off

explanation.surface: Setting out without eating anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' is a phrasal synonym for LAUNCH; drop its A.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal is a specific example of a meal.

clue.text: Acts on one's initiative?

parts.note: Acts here are parliamentary statutes, so this is someone on whose initiative laws get made

explanation.surface: Someone who behaves on their own initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts' reads as a verb; it is a noun, as in Acts of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislator is a person whose initiative brings Acts of Parliament into being.

clue.text: Clubs, perhaps, where naval officers assemble?

definitions.meaning: clubs is one suit of four, so a quarter of a pack of cards
the rear upper deck of a warship, reserved for officers

explanation.surface: Golf clubs or social clubs, maybe, where navy officers meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs are one of four suits, a quarter of a deck; and this is the officers' area on a ship.

clue.text: Sanction accepted by the old couple

indicators.note: the sanction is taken inside the old word, signalling a container

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
to OK something is to sanction it

explanation.surface: Approval granted by the elderly pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of oxen yoked together is a yoke, so the noun can mean a couple.

clue.text: TV presenter who winds up relay?

definitions.meaning: the main newsreader who links a broadcast together
the runner who takes the last leg of a relay race

explanation.surface: A television host who brings a broadcast relay to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both the lead news presenter and the final runner in a relay team.

clue.text: Women soldiers linked -to king's destruction

parts.note: WRAC was the Women's Royal Army Corps, a former British army unit
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Female troops connected with a monarch's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: WRAC was the British army's women's corps until 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack means ruin, as in wrack and ruin, a variant of wreck.

clue.text: Most hi-tech specialist finally probing cardiac condition

indicators.note: the letter probes into the phrase, going inside it

parts.note: the condition of one's heart, read literally as a state of heart

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of specialist

explanation.surface: A top consultant's last word on a heart patient, using the newest technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the most advanced technology currently available, hence most hi-tech.

clue.text: Junior flyer whose 1 across is dispensable

definitions.text: Junior flyer whose 1 across is dispensable

parts.words: Junior flyer whose 1 across is dispensable
parts.note: the 1 across word sits inside this low RAF rank, and removing it still leaves a word for a flyer

explanation.surface: A lowly pilot whose skill nobody needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is CRAFT; remove it and the rank still leaves AIRMAN, another flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank in the Royal Air Force names a junior flyer.

clue.text: Publicists take time accepting fair regulation

indicators.note: the publicists take in the word for fair, signalling a container

parts.note: admen are advertising people, publicists
just means fair

explanation.surface: Advertising people take a moment to agree a fair rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulating something, as with a dial, is making an adjustment to it.

clue.text: Yours and mine take some time, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals the word for a length of time is spoken, dropping its h

parts.note: hours are some length of time

explanation.surface: Yours and mine will take a while, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours and mine together belong to us, so they are our possessions as a pronoun.

clue.text: A French fellow returned and sinned without hindrance

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: returned means the fellow's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, a fellow
erred means sinned

explanation.surface: A Frenchman came back and did wrong, unimpeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhindered and undeterred both describe pressing on with nothing stopping you.

clue.text: Speak clearly, having dined with sister in City area

indicators.note: the sister goes in the postcode, signalling a container

parts.note: EC1 is a London postcode district in and near the City, read as ECI
a nun is a religious sister
ate means having dined

explanation.surface: Speak plainly after eating with a nun in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 is a London postal district; its 1 is read as the letter I. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce words distinctly is to speak them clearly.

clue.text: Husband leaves chapel with case for palm seed

indicators.note: leaves means the husband's letter departs from the chapel word

parts.note: a Bethel is a nonconformist chapel
a case is an eccentric person, a nut

explanation.surface: A husband walks out of chapel carrying a seed box.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'case' here is an oddball, a nut, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The areca palm's seed is chewed in Asia under this name.

clue.text: Old American poet initially inspiring wonder

indicators.note: initially means the poet comes first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: Andrew Marvell was a 17th-century English poet

explanation.surface: An ancient American versifier sparks amazement from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marvellous is wonderful, causing amazement.

clue.text: More than half a violinist's list of options

indicators.note: more than half signals keeping four of the violinist's seven letters

parts.note: Yehudi Menuhin was a famous violinist

explanation.surface: Most of a fiddler's choices on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's card listing dishes, or a computer's set of choices.

clue.text: Conservative gives up censure for physical punishment

indicators.note: gives up means the Conservative's letter is surrendered from the word

parts.note: chiding is censure, a telling-off

explanation.surface: A Tory stops scolding in favour of corporal punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating or thrashing is called a hiding, a physical punishment.

clue.text: Chirpy type possibly in Nancy's game?

definitions.text: Chirpy type possibly in Nancy's game?

parts.words: Chirpy type possibly in Nancy's game?
parts.note: a chirping insect from Nancy, a city in France, describes a simple garden bat-and-ball game

explanation.surface: A cheerful person playing a game with someone called Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy is a city in France, not a woman; the chirpy type is an insect, and the game is a children's form of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's informal cricket game where the batter's legs are the wicket.

clue.text: Marker finally underwritten with mostly African capital

indicators.note: mostly means the capital loses its last letter

parts.note: Cairo is the capital of Egypt

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of underwritten

explanation.surface: A highlighter pen is finally insured with most of an African city's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of stones raised as a landmark or memorial is a marker.

clue.text: Man briefly involved in classical economics

indicators.note: involved in means the name is tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: A brief man embroiled in old-school economic theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Alexander, a man's name given briefly.

clue.text: Unhelpful answer leaving bitter taste?

parts.note: a dud is slang for something useless, and this sour citrus fruit leaves a sharp taste

explanation.surface: A useless reply that leaves a sour feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud or failure is slangily called a lemon, a sour fruit.

clue.text: Dull : prisoner pinches key, returning home

indicators.note: pinches means the prisoner grips the other letters inside

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner
A is a musical key

indicators.note: returning means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A dreary convict steals a key on his way home.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless or spiritless, so inanimate can mean dull.

clue.text: Wartime pilot giving excellent service in court

definitions.meaning: a flying ... shot down many enemy aircraft

explanation.surface: A war flyer serves superbly on the tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fighter pilot with many kills and a tennis serve the receiver cannot touch.

clue.text: Spry flower arranger's attitude following scam

definitions.note: the clue's possessive 's is a link meaning has, so the definition is her first name

indicators.note: following means the attitude comes after the scam

parts.note: a con is a scam
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A nimble florist's approach after a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spry' looks like 'nimble'; it is Constance Spry, the famous British florist.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance Spry was a celebrated British flower arranger and cookery writer.

clue.text: Outburst of emotion about English company

definitions.note: company here means a visitor, one person

indicators.note: about means the outburst goes round the English letter

parts.note: a gust is a sudden outburst of feeling

explanation.surface: Someone's feelings erupt around an English firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Having company means having a visitor in your home.
